name: Observable Universe
description: Everything close enough that its light has reached us since the Big Bang - about 93 billion light-years across.

name: Boötes Void
description: One of the largest known cosmic voids: a nearly empty region ~330 million light-years across in the direction of Boötes.

name: Laniakea Supercluster
description: The galaxy supercluster that contains the Milky Way (printed on the chart as 'LANIKEA').

name: El Gordo (ACT-CL J0102-4915)
description: A massive pair of colliding galaxy clusters about 7 billion light-years away - one of the heaviest distant clusters known.

name: Milky Way
description: Our home galaxy, a barred spiral about 100,000 light-years across.

name: Small Magellanic Cloud
description: A dwarf galaxy orbiting the Milky Way, visible to the naked eye from the Southern Hemisphere.

name: Globular clusters
description: Dense, spherical swarms of hundreds of thousands of old stars orbiting a galaxy.

name: TON 618
description: A hyper-luminous quasar powered by one of the most massive black holes known.

name: Cygnus A
description: A powerful radio galaxy whose central supermassive black hole drives jets hundreds of thousands of light-years long.

name: Sagittarius A*
description: The supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2022.

name: LB-1
description: A binary system announced in 2019 as hosting a surprisingly heavy stellar black hole; the claim has since been disputed.

name: V616 Monocerotis (A0620-00)
description: Probably V616 Monocerotis, one of the nearest known stellar-mass black holes (~3,000 light-years away).

name: Primordial black hole
description: Unlabelled icon on the Schwarzschild line inside the 'primordial black holes*' band: a hypothetical black hole formed in the early universe.

name: Neutron star
description: Unlabelled small dark sphere (tentative): a collapsed stellar core ~20 km across, denser than an atomic nucleus.

name: White dwarfs
description: Unlabelled white spheres (tentative): Earth-sized remnants of Sun-like stars, supported by electron degeneracy pressure.

name: Sun
description: Our star: a G-type main-sequence star holding 99.8% of the Solar System's mass.

name: Red dwarfs
description: Unlabelled red spheres (tentative): small cool stars, the most common kind in the galaxy. The 'STARS & PLANETS' arrow points here.

name: Brown dwarf
description: Unlabelled banded sphere (tentative): a 'failed star' of ~13-80 Jupiter masses, too light to fuse hydrogen.

name: Jupiter
description: The largest planet, more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

name: Saturn
description: Unlabelled ringed planet: the gas giant whose average density is lower than water's.

name: Uranus
description: Unlabelled cyan planet: the ice giant that rotates on its side.

name: Neptune
description: Unlabelled blue planet: the outermost ice giant.

name: Earth
description: Our home planet - the densest planet in the Solar System.

name: Venus
description: Unlabelled tan planet with an arrow pointing at Earth (tentative: Venus, Earth's near-twin in size).

name: Mercury
description: Unlabelled grey planet (tentative): the smallest planet.

name: Mars
description: Unlabelled orange planet (tentative): about half Earth's diameter.

name: Moon
description: Earth's natural satellite, about a quarter of Earth's diameter.

name: Pluto
description: Unlabelled pale body with an arrow pointing at the Moon (tentative: Pluto).

name: Ceres
description: Unlabelled small grey body (tentative): the largest object in the asteroid belt.

name: Enceladus
description: A small icy moon of Saturn that sprays water from a subsurface ocean.

name: Phobos
description: The larger of Mars's two small, lumpy moons.

name: Deimos
description: The smaller, outer moon of Mars.

name: 25143 Itokawa
description: A peanut-shaped rubble-pile asteroid sampled by Japan's Hayabusa probe in 2005.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza
description: The largest of the Giza pyramids, built around 2560 BCE.

name: Sphere (Las Vegas)
description: A spherical entertainment venue opened in 2023, wrapped in LED panels - 157 m wide and 112 m tall.

name: Tree
description: Unlabelled tree icon between the Sphere and the whale; its position (~1e6 kg, ~11 m) matches a giant sequoia, the most massive tree species.

name: Blue whale
description: The largest animal known to have ever lived, up to ~30 m long.

name: Hippopotamus
description: Unlabelled hippopotamus beside the blue whale.

name: Humans
description: Homo sapiens - a typical adult is about 1.7 m tall and 70 kg.

name: Soccer ball
description: Unlabelled football (soccer ball); a regulation size-5 ball is ~22 cm across and ~430 g.

name: Hedgehog
description: A small spiny mammal, typically 15-30 cm long.

name: US penny
description: A US one-cent coin: 19.05 mm across, 2.5 g.

name: Ladybug
description: A small beetle (family Coccinellidae), typically 5-8 mm long.

name: Grain of salt
description: A single crystal of table salt, about 0.3 mm on a side. It sits on the 1 Planck-mass line.

name: Red blood cell
description: A disc-shaped cell ~7.5 µm across that carries oxygen around the body.

name: Bacterium
description: A single-celled microbe; E. coli is about 2 µm long and weighs about a picogram.

name: Virus
description: A virus particle - SARS-CoV-2, for example, is about 100 nm across and weighs about a femtogram.

name: RNA strand
description: A strand of ribonucleic acid; its size depends entirely on its length, so values are representative.

name: Oxygen atom
description: Element 8, the third most abundant element in the universe.

name: Helium atom
description: Element 2, mostly forged in the first minutes after the Big Bang.

name: Fundamental particles
description: Quarks, leptons and bosons - this corner of the triangle is expanded in the 'Fundamental Particles' inset.

name: X and Y bosons
description: Hypothetical bosons of grand unified theories, near 10^24 eV on the energy axis; never observed.

name: Dark exoplanets
description: Marked hypothetical on the chart and drawn as a question-mark icon; no position is physically implied.
